newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Triodos Bank triples shareholders' equity.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Triodos Bank triples shareholders' equity.

text.p: Unlisted Dutch Triodos Bank NV said on Thursday its shareholders' equity had trebled to more than 60 million guilders by the end of 1996.
The bank, which bases its policy not only on financial grounds but also on ethical motives, said it had about 3,500 stakeholders, both private investors and institutions.
Triodos said last September it intended to raise its share capital by issuing non-voting shares in order to finance its growing activities.
Dutch institutions who took up Triodos shares were Rabobank Nederland, bank-insurance group Achmea, Friesland Bank, insurer Reaal and Commercial Union subsidiary Delta Lloyd.
These unlisted institutions each took a 7.5 percent stake. Added to this, pension funds PGGM and ABP took stakes of 7.5 and five percent respectively.
Triodos Bank said Belgian CERA Bank had bought an interest of 1.6 percent and Belgian insurer Mercator&Noordstar now held 3.3 percent of Triodos' shares.
"Triodos intends to approach the Belgian private investors through a share issue in the course of 1997," the bank said in a statement.
Triodos Bank has outlets in the Netherlands, Britain and Belgium.
